narrative.overview:
The direction is AGENTS.md §4's, adopted in 2026-10: a developer keeps Demeteo open all day to supervise agents, so the chrome recedes and the work and its state carry the screen. Colour is spent only on meaning, with one accent, indigo "Signal" (decision 61), for primary actions, selection and focus. Depth is a solid surface step with a 1px hairline rather than an effect, and type is set in sentence case at 11px or more. The benchmarks are developer tools (Linear, Zed, Ghostty, GitHub Primer). The retired direction, "dark neon glassmorphism", is named in §4 as the look a generator reaches for by default.

The shipped code is partway there. The parts that already fit are structural: one status vocabulary (`src/lib/runStatus.ts`) with violet taken out of it, a motion budget that keeps infinite animation to small liveness marks, cascade layers in `src/App.css` so a utility beside a class takes effect, and, since branch `design/surfaces`, solid surfaces: a panel, a raised layer for whatever floats, and a nested card, each with a hairline, one shadow token (the raised layer's), and no blur except on controls floating over a live canvas. Much of the rest is still the old look: the accent is stock violet-500/600 rather than Signal, glows mark status dots, accent bars and primary buttons, decorative blur blobs sit behind status screens, and labels are uppercase mono with wide tracking. The Drift section lists these as follow-up PRs.

It is an Operate tool, and density shows it. The commonest text sizes are 12px (`text-xs`, 408 uses), hand-set 11px (371) and 10px (289). Machine output (ids, costs, token counts, statuses, paths) is set in Fira Code and headings in Outfit. There is no light theme and no theme switch.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-only. Surfaces sit between the well (#050608) and panel hover (#191e29), never lighter.
Colour is meaning. `runStatus.ts` maps every run status to one of five status hues; neither the accent nor violet names a status.
One accent for primary actions, selection and focus: stock violet as shipped, indigo "Signal" as decided (not shipped).

Three solid surface classes, each stating its own hairline and radius: `.panel` (77 call sites in 41 files), `.raised` for menus, dialogs and toasts (33 in 27), and `.nested-card` to group content inside either.
Mono-heavy and dense, with an ungoverned type scale (14 arbitrary text sizes).
Depth is a solid surface step plus a hairline, and only the raised layer casts a shadow. Coloured glow is still shipped on status marks and buttons (Drift 2.1).
Motion is budgeted for cost: `data-motion="paused"` freezes everything while the window is unfocused.

rules.name: The Colour-Is-Meaning Rule
rules.body: Neutral greys do everything that is not a status, an action, a selection or focus. A status colour always ships with a label or icon, because hue alone carries no state (WCAG 2.2 AA is the target).

rules.name: The Accent-Is-Not-A-Status Rule
rules.body: The accent marks primary actions, selection and focus, never a status, and neither does violet, which sits too close to it. `runStatus.ts` still exports a `violet` tone in `RunStatusTone` for non-status accents; every use of it is drift (2.5).

rules.name: The Amber-Is-A-Human Rule
rules.body: Amber means a human is needed and nothing else. "Needs you" is derived from a settled amber status, so an amber status that needs nobody is a bug. Amber is the one hue allowed to call for attention after it settles: three pulses, then it rests lit.

rules.name: The Three-Ladder Rule
rules.body: Every hue is spelled at fixed strengths in `runStatus.ts`: chip (`/10` fill, `-400` ink, `/20` border, `TONE_CHIP`), rail badge (`/20` fill, `-300` ink, `/30` border, `/40` for amber and ruby, `TONE_BADGE`), foreground (`TONE_TEXT`) and a row's left accent at `/60` (`TONE_BORDER_L`).

rules.name: The Machine-Speaks-Mono Rule
rules.body: Anything a machine produced (ids, paths, statuses, counts, costs, durations) is set in Fira Code. Human prose stays Inter.

rules.name: The Primitive-Owns-Its-Type Rule
rules.body: `Chip` and `FieldLabel` refuse casing and typography props, so the pills and labels read as one family and change in one place. As shipped both are uppercase and tracked, which §4 retires; fixing the primitive fixes every call site.

rules.name: The Name-The-Role Rule
rules.body: A font key names a role (`--font-heading`), never a face. A utility naming a face with no `@theme` key compiles to nothing and silently inherits Inter, so `scripts/check-classes.mjs` gates it.

rules.name: The Sentence-Case Rule
rules.body: Labels and headings are sentence case, and copy is translatable: no sentence built by concatenation, no meaning carried by letter case.

rules.name: The Surface-Step Rule
rules.body: Depth comes from which of three solid surfaces an element sits on, each with a 1px hairline. A card is the panel surface; a menu or dialog is the raised one.

rules.name: The Blur-Only-On-Overlays Rule
rules.body: Backdrop blur belongs only to a translucent control floating over live content (the canvas zoom controls and legends, the terminal status overlay), never to a card, a rail or a header, and never under an opaque raised surface, where it shows nothing and still costs WebKitGTK a frame per scroll.

rules.name: The No-Panel-In-Panel Rule
rules.body: A card inside a panel or a dialog is a `.nested-card` (no fill, a hairline, 12px radius, no blur, no shadow), never a second panel, so it groups content on either surface without reading as a third. A field filling a panel (canvas, stream log) is a `.panel-field`: well fill, no border, no radius.

rules.name: The No-Blur-On-Scrims Rule
rules.body: A full-window scrim never takes `backdrop-blur`. Every dialog scrim, `Modal`'s default included, is a flat `bg-black/60`, because a blurred scrim re-blurs the whole window every frame something animates beneath it.

rules.name: The One-Panel-Radius Rule
rules.body: Every panel-level surface is 12px (`--radius-panel`), and a call site never re-spells it. A card, a canvas well and a banner are the same object at different depths, and a second value reads as a mistake. Smaller radii belong to controls.

rules.name: The Motion Budget Rule
rules.body: An infinite animation claims something is still happening, so it belongs only on a small liveness dot or an in-flight spinner, and on WebKitGTK any running animation costs a core. It animates opacity only, never `box-shadow` or `transform`. All animation pauses while the window is unfocused (`data-motion="paused"`) and stops under `prefers-reduced-motion`. A pulse that is not liveness must be finite. The only shimmer is an indeterminate progress bar.

dos: **Do** read token values from `src/styles/tokens.css`; never hard-code hex.
**Do** pick a status hue through `runStatusMeta` / `TONE_CHIP` / `TONE_TEXT` / `TONE_BADGE` / `TONE_BORDER_L`, render status pills with `Chip`, and ship every status colour with a label or icon.
**Do** keep the accent for primary actions, selection and focus, with a white label on an accent fill. New code waits for the Signal tokens rather than adding stock `violet-*`.
**Do** use amber only for "a human is needed", and let its pulse run three beats, then rest lit.

**Do** use `.panel` for a panel, `.raised` for anything floating (menu, popover, dialog, toast), `.nested-card` for a group inside either, and `.panel-field` for a field filling a panel, and keep their fill, border, radius and shadow unspelled at the call site.
**Do** keep blur for translucent controls floating over live content (canvas zoom controls and legends, the terminal status overlay); an opaque raised surface takes none.
**Do** write labels and headings in sentence case, at 11px or more, and say Project, not Workspace.
**Do** set machine output (ids, paths, counts, costs, statuses) in Fira Code and headings in `font-heading`.
**Do** put an infinite pulse only on a small liveness dot or spinner, and animate opacity only.
**Do** use `Modal` for overlays: portalled, a flat `bg-black/60` scrim, Escape to close, with a `.raised` body.
**Do** keep inline `style` for geometry (heights, offsets, measured widths).
donts: **Don't** build a light theme or place these surfaces on a light ground.
**Don't** add glow shadows or `text-shadow`, or a gradient fill on a button or text.
**Don't** add decorative blurred blobs, sparkle icons as ornament, `hover:scale`, or shimmer outside an indeterminate progress bar.
**Don't** blur a card, a rail, a header or a raised surface, nest a panel in a panel, or blur a full-window scrim.
**Don't** use all-caps letter-spaced labels or text under 11px.
**Don't** pass a colour into `Chip`, or hand-write `bg-<hue>-500/10 text-<hue>-400` for a status.
**Don't** give the accent or violet a status, use violet as decoration, or give amber a state that needs nobody.
**Don't** put design tokens in `style=` props or raw hex.
**Don't** name a font utility after a face (`font-outfit`); a key with no `@theme` entry silently renders Inter.
**Don't** copy a pattern because it sits nearby; check it against the Drift list first.

drift.text: **Overlays hand-rolled instead of `Modal`.** Breaks: one raised surface for menus and dialogs, reached one way. Evidence: `fixed inset-0` = 13/13, of which 12 are overlays outside `ui/Modal.tsx` (`<Modal\b` = 12/10): GateView, McpConsentView, CommandPalette, DocsPanel, CommandSelector, EnvModal, StartFeatureModal, ShortcutHelp, the ProvidersPage "provider in use" confirm, AddressFindingsLaunch, ProviderSettings and NewTerminalMenu's centred variant. All now have a `.raised` body over a `bg-black/60` scrim, but each spells its own scrim and dismissal. NewProjectView's repo picker and WorkflowBuilder's unsaved-changes guard use `absolute inset-0`, so they cover only their own view; `Modal` is portalled and would cover the window. Fix: route the 12 through `Modal`; decide whether the two scoped ones stay scoped.

**ShortcutHelp's group cards are a fourth surface.** Breaks: a card inside a dialog is a `.nested-card`. Evidence: ShortcutHelp.tsx renders each shortcut group as `rounded-xl border border-white/5 bg-[#0d0f14]/40` inside its `.raised` body (one class string, repeated per group). Fix: `.nested-card`.

**DocsPanel's panes are darker bands.** Breaks: no band darker than the surface it sits on. Evidence: inside DocsPanel's `.raised` body, the nav is `bg-[#08090c]/40` and the content pane `bg-[#08090c]/60`. Fix: drop both fills; the nav keeps its hairline divider.

**WorkflowBuilder's root is an untokened near-black.** Breaks: three solid surfaces, values in `tokens.css`. Evidence: the WorkflowBuilder root is `bg-[#0b0d12]`, between the app and sidebar surfaces with no token of its own. Fix: `bg-surface-app`, or no fill.

**AddressFindingsLaunch's card is hand-spelled.** Breaks: one panel class. Evidence: its in-flow launch card is `rounded-xl border border-white/5 bg-black/20`, a translucent card with no class. Fix: `.nested-card` if its host is a panel, else `.panel`.

**Chrome spells the hairline by hand.** Breaks: the edge is a token. Evidence: the outer edges of TopBar, both ProjectRail asides, FeatureHeader, VersionDrawer, ConfigPanel and WorkflowBuilder's drawer spell `border-white/5` (7 sites), as do their inner dividers (10 more) and WorkflowList's rows on `bg-surface-panel` (2), read one by one. Tree-wide, `\bborder(-[trblxy])?-white/5\b` = 246/101 against `\bborder-hairline\b` = 1/1 (the top-bar search). Same value, so nothing renders differently. Fix: `border-hairline` on the chrome, then sweep the rest.

**12px spelled without the panel token.** Breaks: the panel radius is `--radius-panel`. Evidence: `\brounded-xl\b` = 62/41 (`rg -c '\brounded-xl\b' src` = 63/42 with one comment line), none on the same line as `.panel`, `.raised` or `.nested-card`. They are mostly panel-like boxes (artifact wells, notices, canvas ticket nodes, toasts, ShortcutHelp's cards from 1.9) plus some icon tiles. `--radius-panel` is a `:root` property, not a `@theme` key, so no `rounded-panel` utility exists. Fix: move each onto a surface class, or expose the radius as a utility for the ones that are not surfaces.

**Shadows cast outside `.raised`.** Breaks: only the raised surface casts a shadow. Evidence: neutral shadows at call sites, `(?<![\w:-])shadow-(sm|md|lg|xl|2xl)\b|shadow-\[0_(?!0_)[^\]]*\]` = 13/9 (no `shadow-2xl` left), among them canvas nodes `shadow-lg shadow-black/30` and artifact wells `shadow-lg`. Fix: delete in-flow shadows; decide whether a canvas node is raised (and casts `--shadow-raised`) or a panel.

**Translucent near-black fills.** Breaks: three solid surfaces. Evidence: `bg-\[#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}\]/\d+` = 36/27, 16 distinct values, led by `bg-[#0d0f14]/90` ×6 (Ask and Discovery composers and the 1.15 footers), `bg-[#08090c]/40` ×5 (read-only fields in StrategyTab and HarnessModelPicker, DocsPanel's nav) and `bg-[#050608]/85` ×4 (artifact wells); also WorkflowList's and CodeEditorView's side panes at `/50`. It includes 1.9, 1.10, and 1.15's footers and translucent bodies. Fix: the solid `surface-*` utilities, or no fill where the host already has one.

**Stock violet is the accent.** Breaks: the accent is indigo "Signal" (decision 61), and violet names nothing. Evidence: every `violet-` utility is to migrate or remove: `\bviolet-` = 446/106. Split by role: solid fills `(?<![\w/-])bg-violet-(500|600|700)(?![\w/])` = 41/21 plus state fills `(hover|active|disabled):bg-violet-` = 44/30 (primary buttons); focus `(focus|focus-visible|focus-within):[\w-]*violet` = 19/11; text `(?<![\w:-])text-violet-` = 136/74; borders `(?<![\w:-])border-(l-)?violet-` = 80/56; tints `(?<![\w:-])bg-violet-\d+/` = 84/50; `rgba(139,92,246…)` literals in TSX = 31/23 (mostly glows, 2.1). In CSS: `--accent-purple` and `--accent-purple-glow` and `--border-glass-focus` in `tokens.css`; in `App.css`, `var(--accent-purple)` ×3 (scrollbar thumb while dragged, agent chat-bubble sender, `.btn-primary`), `rgba(139,92,246,…)` ×6 (agent chat bubble, `.btn-primary` border and glow, progress shimmer, two pinned utilities), `#7c3aed` and the caret's `#a78bfa`. Which of these are action, selection or focus (migrate to Signal) and which are decoration or status (2.5, remove) takes reading each site; the fill, focus and selection counts above are the migrate set. Fix: once the Signal tokens land as `@theme` colours, replace action, selection and focus uses with them, then delete `--accent-purple*`.

**Glow shadows.** Breaks: never glow shadows. Evidence: `shadow-\[0_0_[^\]]*\]` = 94/38, 59 distinct strings; by colour, violet 31, emerald 21, cyan 18, amber 9, ruby 5, slate 3, other 7. They include `StatusBadge`'s `TONE_DOT`, `PipelineCard`'s `TONE_ACCENT` and primary buttons (`hover:shadow-\[0_0_` = 7/5). The gate and artifact modal halos and the two black ones went with the raised surface on branch `design/surfaces`. `App.css` adds five more: `.animate-pulse-glow` (static cyan halo; 16/12 uses), `.animate-pulse-glow-amber` (2/2), and the focus glows on `.input-field` and `.chat-input` and the hover glow on `.btn-primary`. `tokens.css` keeps four `--accent-*-glow` values, one of them used. Fix: delete the glows; dots and bars go solid, focus becomes a ring, and the `--accent-*-glow` tokens go.

**Gradient primary button.** Breaks: no gradient fills on buttons. Evidence: `.btn-primary` in `App.css` is `linear-gradient(135deg, var(--accent-purple), #7c3aed)` with a hover glow; `\bbtn-primary\b` = 15/14, all in `ask/`, `discovery/` and their modals. `AskCanvasNodeInspector` has one more gradient button (`bg-gradient-to-br from-violet-600 to-violet-700`). Fix: a solid Signal fill (`#5a60c2`, hover `#6269cc`, white label), the same one 2.3's primitive uses.

**Two primary spellings, no primitive.** Breaks: one primary action treatment (inferred from §4's "the accent = primary actions"; §4 does not name a Button primitive). Evidence: inline `\bbg-violet-600\b` = 35/21 and `\bhover:bg-violet-500\b` = 38/29 beside the 15 `.btn-primary`. Fix: a `Button` primitive in `src/components/ui/` with primary (Signal fill, white label), secondary, ghost and destructive variants; it is the natural place for 2.0's migration.

**Focus and selection are cyan.** Breaks: the accent = selection and focus. Evidence: `focus(-visible|-within)?:border-cyan-` = 81/32 against `…:border-violet-` = 19/11; `focus(-visible)?:ring-cyan` = 4/4 (including `SegmentedControl`), `ring-violet` = 0. `TabBar` selects with `border-cyan-500` plus `TONE_TEXT.cyan`, and `SegmentedControl` with `TONE_CHIP.cyan`. In `App.css`, `::selection`, `select option:checked` and the scrollbar thumb on hover are cyan. The 19 violet focus borders are drift too (2.0). Fix: one shared focus ring in Signal (`#6e78db`), and Signal selected states (border `#6972c0`, tint `rgba(90,96,194,.16)`) in `TabBar`, `SegmentedControl` and `App.css`.

**Violet still names states and decorates.** Breaks: neither the accent nor violet is a status, colour is spent only on meaning, and status hues resolve through `runStatus.ts`. Evidence: `tone=["']violet["']|tone:\s*['"]violet['"]|TONE_(CHIP|TEXT|BADGE|BORDER_L)\.violet|\['violet'\]` = 27/17. Among them: `discoveryProgress.ts` ("Interviewing"), `askLifecycle.ts` ("Asking", "Open"), `ticketPresentation.ts` (the "Ready" lane), `StorageProjectCard`/`StoragePanel` ("Reclaimable"), canvas node kinds in `canvas/types.ts`, and model or workflow names as violet `Chip`s (`PipelineCard`, `FeatureHeader`, `AskThreadCard`, `DiscoveryCard`, discovery views). `syncPanel.ts`'s violet entries are actions ("Sync", "Resolve with agent"), so they move to the accent (2.0) rather than going away. `App.css` tints the agent's chat bubble violet. `HeaderNavItem` tints icons violet, cyan or amber by an `accent` prop (4 uses in `TopBar`). Fix: lifecycle states to cyan or slate by meaning, names to slate chips, header icons and the agent bubble neutral; then drop `violet` from `RunStatusTone`.

**Amber for states that need nobody.** Breaks: amber = a human is needed, and only that. Evidence: amber tone references outside `runStatus.ts` (`(tone|accent)\s*[:=]\s*['"]amber['"]|: 'amber'`) = 25/16. Read one by one, these need nobody: `activitySync.ts` "reconnecting", `decomposeReview.ts` "Revised" and "blocked by …", `ticketPresentation.ts` "Blocked" ("waiting on an edge"), the `AskThreadCard` "network" chip, and `harnessVerdict.ts`'s "unrunnable" (multi-line, not in the count). Gate nodes, credential failures, PR conflicts and "Undecided — left for you" arguably do. Fix: in-motion states to cyan, dependency and change kinds to slate; §4 needs a home for "warning".

**Three reds and off-palette hues.** Breaks: ruby = failed or destructive; colour only for meaning. Evidence: ruby classes 289/73, rose 92/19, red 29/5 (`(?<![\w-])(text|bg|border|ring|from|to|via|fill|stroke|shadow|outline)-<hue>-`). Rose carries GateView's Abort and "decision blocked". `App.css` pins `text-red-400`, `bg-red-500/10` and two `border-red-500/*`. Yellow, orange and blue add 12/4 (`CodeEditorView` git letters and folder icons, `ErrorToast`'s orange accent, `GeneralTab`'s unpushed chip, a yellow button in `WorkflowList`). Fix: rose and red to ruby; orange and yellow to amber only where a human is needed, else slate.

**Emerald for healthy machines.** Breaks: emerald = finished well (§4 no longer names "healthy"). Evidence: `StatusBadge`'s `NON_RUN_TONES` maps `idle` and `active` to emerald. Fix: decide whether a healthy machine is "finished well" or slate, and record it in §4.

**Decorative blurred blobs.** Breaks: never decorative blurred blobs. Evidence: `rounded-full[^"`]*(?<![-\w])blur-(\[\d+px\]|xl|2xl|3xl)` = 20 lines in 11 files: `ProjectSettingsShell` ×5, `EmptyStateCard` ×4, `ProjectHome` ×2, `NewProjectView` ×2, and one each in `RemoteRunInbox`, `WizardShell`, `ProviderSettings`, `PreferencesScreen`, `CreateFromZeroWizard`, `MachinesView`, `ProvidersPage`. Fix: delete them.

**Sparkles as ornament.** Breaks: never sparkle icons as ornament. Evidence: `<Sparkles\b` = 12/10 (`ProjectRail` ×2, `EmptyStateCard` ×2, `NewProjectView`, `CreateFromZeroWizard`, `GateView`, `AgentBadge`, `StartFeatureModal`, `ShortcutHelp`, `NewTerminalMenu`, `StartSessionButton`). Most sit beside a text label that already says what the control does. `AgentBadge` in compact mode shows only the sparkle, so there it may carry meaning. Fix: use the icon of the thing (a plus, a terminal, a file) or none.

**Gradient ornament.** Breaks: no gradient fills on buttons or text (strictly, these are on tiles, avatars and washes, which §4's wording does not name; they are ornament either way). Evidence: `\bbg-gradient-to-[a-z]+` = 12/8: icon tiles (`MachinesView` ×2, `PreferencesScreen`, `EmptyStateCard`), avatars (`AccountMenu`, `ProvidersPage`), a hover wash on a `ProjectHome` card, `ShortcutHelp`'s header bands ×2, the `EmptyStateCard` CTA overlay and sheen, and the `AskCanvasNodeInspector` button (2.2). The two `radial-gradient` uses are canvas dot grids and are functional. Fix: flat fills.

**`hover:scale`.** Breaks: never `hover:scale`. Evidence: `(?<![\w-])hover:scale-` = 4/1 and `group-hover:scale-` = 4/1, all in the `EmptyStateCard` hero tiles. Fix: a border or background shift on hover.

**Shimmer outside progress.** Breaks: shimmer only on an indeterminate progress bar. Evidence: the `EmptyStateCard` sample-project button sweeps a `via-white/10` gradient across itself on hover. The one allowed shimmer, `.animate-progress-shimmer` (1/1, `TerminalStatusOverlay`), runs its gradient through violet, which is decoration. Fix: delete the sheen; make the progress bar cyan (in motion).

**The first-run hero.** `EmptyStateCard` combines 3.1–3.5, two glows and a gradient icon tile, and its copy ("a modern, premium control center…") breaks PRODUCT.md's binding voice (direct, no hype). Fix: rebuild it as one solid panel, three plain actions and plain copy; it is the first thing a new user sees.

**All-caps letter-spaced labels.** Breaks: never all-caps letter-spaced labels; meaning not carried by letter case. Evidence: `\buppercase\b` = 275/108, and 274 of those lines also carry positive tracking (`tracking-(wide|wider|widest|\[[0-9.]+(em|px)\])` = 295/115 overall; `tracking-wider` 178, `tracking-widest` 66, `tracking-wide` 35, six arbitrary values). The primitives multiply it: `Chip` is always `uppercase tracking-wide` (`<Chip\b` = 64/24), `FieldLabel` is `uppercase tracking-wider` (49/17), `SectionCard` too (0 uses), and `App.css`'s `.chat-bubble-sender`. Fix: sentence case in `Chip` and `FieldLabel` first (two one-line changes), then sweep the hand-rolled ones.

**Text under 11px.** Breaks: never text under 11px. Evidence: `(?<![\w-])text-\[(?:[0-9]|10)(?:\.\d+)?px\]` = 345/125: `text-[10px]` 288/113, `text-[9px]` 53/28, `text-[10.5px]` 3, `text-[9.5px]` 1. `Chip size="sm"` is 10px (`<Chip\b[^>]*size="sm"` = 47/19 on one line) and `RailBadge` is 10px. Fix: raise `Chip` `sm` and `RailBadge` to 11px, then replace 9px and 10px with an 11px step.

**Ungoverned type scale.** Breaks: no rule directly; it is why 4.2 recurs. Evidence: 14 arbitrary sizes (`text-[11px]` 371/119, `[13px]` 42, `[12px]` 16, which equals `text-xs`, `[11.5px]` 15, `[12.5px]` 4, plus one-offs) and no type-size tokens. Fix: a small size scale as `@theme` keys in `tokens.css`.

**Title Case strings.** Breaks: sentence case for labels and headings. Evidence (heuristic, so approximate): two or more capitalised words with only short connectives between them, found 71 times as same-line JSX text, 23 as standalone JSX text lines, 14 in `label`/`title`/`aria-label`/`placeholder` attributes and 24 in object-literal `label`/`title` values, about 132 in all. Examples: "Workspace Bootstrap In Progress", "Configure Worktree Strategy", "Copy Complete Output", "Save Changes", "Provider Type", and shortcut and command-palette labels in `src/lib/shortcuts.ts` and `App.tsx`. Some hits are names (product or workflow names). Fix: sentence case, file by file.

**"Workspace" where the noun is Project.** Breaks: PRODUCT.md Vocabulary (the UI says Project); §4's translatable-copy rule. Evidence: `(?<![\w./-])[Ww]orkspaces?(?![\w/-])` on user-facing lines = 57 matches on 55 lines in 19 files; every line was read. About 45 lines name a Project (settings headings, bootstrap screens, the rail's "Workspaces" header, "Delete Workspace"). The other 10 use the word for something else and need their own noun: the app-wide data directory (`PreferencesScreen` ×3), the whole install (`McpConsentView` ×2), a Git host account (`ProvidersPage`), the Discovery pane (`DiscoveryWorkspaceRow`), a feature worktree path (`NewProjectView`), the command palette placeholder (`TopBar`) and the empty-state back label (`parentView.ts`). Fix: rename to Project; give the other 10 their own words.

**"Provider" where the thing is a Git host connection.** Breaks: PRODUCT.md (in code a ProviderInstance is a GitHub or GitLab connection), where the UI noun is still an Open Decision. Evidence: a scripted pass over string literals and JSX text found 48 occurrences on 46 lines in 21 files, a lower bound because multi-line JSX strings are missed (for example `PostReviewComment`'s "using your provider"). Examples: "Source Providers" (`ProvidersPage`, `TopBar` title), "Connect a Provider", "Provider Type", "No Providers Mapped", the wizard step label "Provider". Fix: settle the noun in PRODUCT.md, then rename.
**Redundant `font-sans`.** Breaks: UI text needs no class. Evidence: `\bfont-sans\b` = 24/10, including the root shell in `App.tsx`. Fix: delete.

**Arbitrary hex classes.** Breaks: never raw hex for design tokens. Evidence: `\[#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}\]` = 131/60, 12 distinct values. 83 restate tokens: `#08090c` ×45 (`surface-app`), `#0d0f14` ×21 (`surface-sidebar`), `#050608` ×17 (`surface-well`). 48 are near-blacks with no token: `#050508` ×19, `#0b0d12` ×10, `#0a0c10` ×8, `#0c0d12` ×4, `#12161e` ×3 and four singletons. Fix: replace the 83 with the `surface-*` utilities that branch `design/surfaces` added, and fold the 48 onto the nearest surface.

**Tokens are bypassed.** Breaks: values live in `tokens.css` and are read from there. Evidence: TSX reaches a token only through 10 `bg-[var(--…)]` uses and the surface utilities (`bg-surface-*` 21/14, `border-hairline` 1/1); `--accent-*` and `--text-*` are referenced from TSX zero times. Components colour through palette classes (by 2.7's pattern: cyan 540, violet 439, ruby 289, amber 259, emerald 258). The two neutral ladders disagree: `--text-*` are Tailwind gray (#f3f4f6 / #9ca3af / #6b7280), while components use slate and `text-white` (383), and the root shell sets `text-white` over `body`'s `--text-primary`. Fix: one neutral ladder as tokens; the status hues stay behind `runStatus.ts`'s `TONE_*` maps.

**`style=` props carrying design values.** Breaks: never `style=` for design tokens. Evidence: `style=\{\{` = 20/13, read one by one. The two that set a surface (`ShortcutHelp`, `WizardShell`) are gone (see Resolved). One still carries type: EnvModal's Browse button overrides `.btn-secondary` with `padding: "0 12px", fontSize: "0.8rem"`. The rest are geometry. Fix: a size utility on the EnvModal button.

**Colour values outside `tokens.css`.** Breaks: token values live in `tokens.css`. Evidence: `App.css` still declares 22 hex literals in rules: 11 in the `PINNED UTILITY COLOURS` block (32 utility classes re-declared at Tailwind v3 values) and 11 elsewhere (`.btn-primary`'s `#7c3aed` and `#fff`, the caret's `#a78bfa`, the native-control rules), plus rgba values in `.panel-hover`'s 8% border, `.bubble-code`, the chat bubbles, the scrollbar and the skeleton. Fix: move the values to tokens; whether to keep the v3 pins is a palette decision, per the block's own comment.

**Hex in library themes.** Breaks: no raw hex (lower priority: the libraries need values, not classes). Evidence: `['"]#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}['"]` = 18/3: `TerminalSurface` (xterm theme) ×11, `canvas/flowGraph.ts` ×5, `WorkflowCanvas` ×2. Fix: read them from the CSS custom properties at runtime, or from one exported token map.

**Unused tokens.** Evidence: no `var()` or utility reads `--accent-emerald`, `--accent-ruby`, three of the four `--accent-*-glow`, `--text-muted`, `--text-dark`, `--transition-spring` or `--transition-smooth`. Fix: delete them.

**`!important` native-control rules beat call-site utilities.** Breaks: no raw hex for tokens; a call site's utilities should apply (the reason for PR #250's layers). Evidence: the unlayered rules at the end of `App.css` hold 17 `!important` declarations on `select`, `option`/`optgroup`, `input[type=text|search|email|password|url]`, `textarea` and placeholders (#0a0a0e fill, #e2e8f0 text, #475569 placeholder, a cyan checked option, and on `select` `appearance: none`, a chevron `background-image` and `padding-right: 28px`). A scripted pass over JSX tags found 128 matching fields in 54 files (`select` 45, `input type="text"` 62, `password` 7, `search` 2, `textarea` 12). 98 of them carry a `bg-*` utility and 94 a text-colour utility that never apply, and the 14 using `.input-field` lose its background too. Inputs without a `type` attribute (8) and number inputs (10) are not matched, so they render differently. Moving the rules into `@layer base` would let 31 of the 45 selects' padding utilities (`p-`/`px-`/`pr-`) override the 28px chevron gutter. That it would also lose the chevron `background-image` was reported to me and not verified here. Fix: move the rules to `@layer base` on token colours, give `select` its chevron and gutter through a class or a `pr-7` convention, then remove the dead `bg-*` and text utilities.

**Selection and body font as `!important`.** Evidence: `::selection` is an unlayered `!important` cyan (see 2.4), and the "WebKitGTK / Tauri compatibility layer" re-declares `body`'s font with `!important`, duplicating the `@layer base` rule. Fix: fold both into `@layer base`, with selection in violet.

driftOutsideGroups: **Status vocabularies outside `runStatus.ts`.** §4 says status hues resolve through `runStatus.ts` and nowhere else. About a dozen modules keep their own label→tone tables, reusing its `RunStatusTone` type and `TONE_*` maps: `syncPanel`, `discoveryProgress`, `askLifecycle`, `ticketPresentation`, `decomposeReview`, `activitySync`, `pullRequestRow`, `harnessVerdict`, `staleness` and `pipelineCard` in `src/lib/`, plus `RemoteRunInbox`, `canvas/types`, `StorageProjectCard` and `ReviewFailureCard`. Whether reusing the `TONE_*` maps satisfies "through runStatus.ts" is for §4 to say; 2.5 and 2.6 are where these tables disagree with it.
**No-op animation.** `NotificationBell`'s toast uses `animate-[fadeIn_120ms_ease-out]`, and no `fadeIn` keyframe exists (the keyframe is `fade-in`).

**Stale written guidance.** `.design-sync/conventions.md` still teaches the retired system: violet = "agent working", emerald = "running agent", `style={{ background: 'var(--bg-panel)' }}` for tokens, uppercase `tracking-widest` small labels, `SectionCard` first, and `StatusBadge variant="pill"`, a prop that no longer exists.
